questions.question: Why do AI features need incident runbooks?
options: Because model behavior, retrieval quality, tool calls, cost, and safety controls can fail
Because support teams should improvise every response
questions.explanation: AI operations covers quality, cost, safety, and tool behavior in addition to uptime.

questions.question: Which signal is explicitly part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Quality drift is a core AI operations signal.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked incident triage plan with controls and rationale
questions.explanation: The artifact helps plan incident response controls.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: Rollback paths help contain AI feature incidents.

questions.question: When should an AI incident trigger escalation?
options: When impact, uncertainty, and operational risk signals are high
questions.explanation: High-impact operational issues need clear escalation.

questions.question: What should a postmortem update after an AI incident?
options: Evals, prompts, tools, controls, and runbooks
Nothing; AI incidents are not repeatable
questions.explanation: Postmortems should improve the operating system around the AI feature.
